subject: Dedicated inference — isolation appetite, burst profile & SLA framing
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Arjun Menon <arjun@medalign.com>, Dr. Priya Rao <priya@medalign.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated inference — isolation appetite, burst profile & SLA framing

Thanks for taking the time today — quick recap and next steps so we have alignment.

TL;DR: MediAlign's primary goals are (1) stable low tail latency during peak inference, (2) strong tenant isolation for PHI workloads, and (3) predictable cost for a reserved-capacity path with defined burst behavior. Recommended immediate next step is a scoped dedicated pool + staged canary.

Key pain points you called out:
- P99 latency spikes under concurrent batch runs (alerts from last quarter).
- Multi-tenant interference during overnight model-training bursts that occasionally saturate inference nodes.
- Procurement needs to satisfy HIPAA / PHI isolation controls and evidence for internal audit.

Goals discussed:
- Production SLO target: P95 latency <250ms for typical 256-token requests (we'll profile with exact payloads).
- Baseline committed throughput: ~45 req/s sustained, support for bursts to ~120 req/s for short windows.
- Isolation: logical tenant isolation with dedicated GPU pool; optional single-tenant lanes for PHI-sensitive endpoints.
- Rollout: canary (2–3% traffic) for 2 weeks, then incremental ramp.

Initial recommended configuration (open for your feedback):
- Dedicated pool: 6 x NVIDIA-A100-equivalent vGPUs reserved (baseline).
- Burst capacity: headroom to 2x baseline via burst queueing and pre-warmed instances.
- Quantization & batching profile: aggressive batching at non-peak, adaptive batching during latency-sensitive windows.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to lower-cost compatible variant if capacity saturated.

Commercial and ops notes:
- We attached a short SLA draft for review (MediAlign_SLA_Draft.pdf) and a mutual action plan template (MAP_MediAlign.xlsx). These are starting points; pricing/commit math TBD after you confirm steady-state qps and desired availability window.

Asks / immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm the burst target (120 req/s) and your expected average payload (tokens per request).
2) Confirm whether PHI endpoints require physically single-tenant nodes or logical isolation is sufficient.
3) Share procurement timeline (you mentioned end-of-year cadence).
4) If you can, send your security questionnaire and any SOC2 / HIPAA audit contacts.

Next steps (we'll own scheduling and follow-ups):
- Ben will run a capacity sketch (nodes, GPUs, expected queueing behavior) once we get confirmation of qps/payload.
- Jordan will scope the canary rollout plan and SLO validation tests.
- Mina to circulate SLA draft + MAP and set up a follow-up for technical deep-dive next week.

Attachments: MediAlign_SLA_Draft.pdf (draft), MAP_MediAlign.xlsx (mutual action plan template)

Best,

Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Arjun Menon <arjun@medalign.com>

Cc: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@medalign.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated inference — isolation appetite, burst profile & SLA framing

Thanks Mina — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side after we synced with infra and security: 

- Sustained workload: ~45 req/s average (our dashboard shows this across core hours).
- Typical payload: ~230–300 tokens (varies, callouts are usually <512).
- Burst behavior: can spike to ~110–130 req/s for 2–8 minute windows (traffic pattern tied to customer sync jobs).

On isolation: PHI endpoints are currently processed in a logically isolated namespace, but our compliance team is asking whether physical single-tenant nodes are available as an option (they want verifiable isolation for certain regulated workflows). Logical isolation is acceptable for the majority, but for 2–3 high-risk endpoints we may need physically single-tenant lanes.

Procurement: we are targeting a signed commitment by 2026-12-20. We will need a short statement of evidence for HIPAA controls and an estimated lead time for private pool provisioning.

I attached our internal security questionnaire (MediAlign_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx) — please pass to your security/compliance team and let us know what evidence you can provide.

Also: can you put a ballpark monthly commit range next to the configuration you suggested so we can budget before the procurement meeting? A range is fine (e.g., $X–$Y).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Arjun
Arjun Menon
Head of Platform Engineering, MediAlign Health

Looping in a quick technical checklist from infra perspective (internal only):

- If sustained 45 req/s and burst 120 req/s (8 minute windows), estimate: 6 reserved A100-equivalent nodes as Mina suggested + 2 warm standby instances for burst headroom.
- For physical single-tenant lanes: we can reserve 2 dedicated hosts that do not accept other tenants — leads to ~10–15% provisioning overhead and slightly higher unit cost.
- Autoscaling warm-start: recommend pre-warming 1–2 instances during expected sync windows to avoid cold-start tail latency.
- Observability: need rulebook for p95/p99 alerts and a synthetic load test to validate P95 <250ms at canary scale. Jordan — can you own the test harness?

I’ll produce a back-of-envelope cost estimate once Arjun confirms the final burst window and token profile. Also, request SOC2 artifact pointer from Security for the evidence pack.

Ben

- Burst target: support up to 120–130 req/s for short windows; plan includes 2 warm standbys and autoscale headroom.
- PHI isolation: MediAlign confirms 2 high-risk endpoints will need physically single-tenant lanes; remainder can use logical isolation. We will include the single-tenant option in pricing and runbook.
- SLO: target P95 <250ms (validate at canary).
- Procurement target: signature by 2026-12-20.
